label: Radiation alert

alert.text: Radiation alert: elevated dose rate. Early warning of a solar particle event; shelter early (ALARA).

notes: Peak window of the September 2017 event in hazards.json models.sep_2017_profile. Two rates are RAD measurements (Zeitlin et al. 2018, Table 1, B detector, dose in water, Gale crater, not Jezero): 240 uGy/day before the event (10 uGy/h) and the 718 uGy/day peak (29.92 uGy/h). The steps tagged SIM, 20 uGy/h on the way up and 12 uGy/h on the way down, are our choice, as are the times of every step and the staircase shape (the engine holds each value until the next step) (#295). Outside the event the HUD rate is the RAD background of Hassler et al. 2014, 8.75 uGy/h, from the E detector (tissue-like): the step from 8.75 to 10 uGy/h at the start is a change of detector, not a rise in radiation. The 12-minute duration is a SIM compression for one EVA. The environment runner (src/sim/environmentRunner.js) sums environment.doseRateUgyH into environment.doseUgy over mission time, so the event sets only the rate and the dose this EVA is these rates over the minutes the event plays; the real event added 544 uGy (B detector, water) over about 57 h (hazards.json radiation.sep_2017.event_dose). Shelter is the habitat, the only full-protection shelter in public/data/shelters.json. When it starts, and how fast this timeline runs, comes from the mission the crew's objective defines (src/sim/missions.js, #265): T+720 s and this 12-minute timeline in the full EVA; in the first mission T+95 s at the earliest, 15 s after the storm and outside the 25 m end area, with the timeline compressed to 1 minute (SIM).
